record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For continuous-time linear periodic systems, can one develop effective stabilization algorithms that compute stabilizing solutions directly in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For continuous-time periodic systems, there are no algorithms for efficient computation of frequency responses, stabilisation or pole assignment.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system
\[
\dot x(t) = A(t)x(t) + B(t)u(t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{R},
\]
where $A:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $B:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ are piecewise continuous and $T$-periodic, i.e. $A(t+T)=A(t)$ and $B(t+T)=B(t)$ for some fixed period $T>0$. The pair $(A(\cdot),B(\cdot))$ is assumed to be stabilizable in the periodic sense: there exists a piecewise continuous $T$-periodic feedback gain $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ such that the monodromy matrix $\Phi_{A+BF}(T,0)$ of the closed-loop system $\dot x = (A(t)+B(t)F(t))x$ has spectral radius strictly less than $1$.

Develop an effective numerical algorithm that, working directly in the periodic continuous-time setting (without first reducing the problem to a single time-invariant lifted system or to its discrete-time monodromy representation), computes such a $T$-periodic stabilizing feedback gain $F(\cdot)$. The algorithm should:
(i) take as input numerically tractable representations of $A(\cdot)$ and $B(\cdot)$ (e.g.\ truncated Fourier series, piecewise polynomial samples, or evaluations along one period);
(ii) return a $T$-periodic feedback $F(\cdot)$ in a comparable representation;
(iii) guarantee, under standard regularity hypotheses on $(A,B)$, that the resulting closed-loop monodromy matrix is Schur-stable; and
(iv) be efficient and numerically reliable in the sense that its computational cost and conditioning scale gracefully with $n$, $m$, and the complexity of the representation of $A(\cdot)$, $B(\cdot)$.

Does such an effective stabilization algorithm exist for general continuous-time linear periodic systems?
artifact.status_search_result: There has been substantial progress on stabilization and pole assignment for linear periodic systems. Methods include periodic Lyapunov differential equation–based feedback, variation-of-constant discretization plus sequential pole placement, parametric periodic state feedback for the discrete-time case, and LMI-based approaches. However, most general-purpose continuous-time algorithms still proceed via discretization or lifting; truly direct, efficient, numerically reliable continuous-time periodic stabilization algorithms with the same maturity as the discrete-time case have only partially been developed.

status_evidence.title: Stability analysis and stabilization of linear continuous-time periodic systems by variation-of-constant discretization
status_evidence.snippet: Stabilizing continuous-time periodic systems is addressed by periodically time-varying state feedback via sequential pole assignment after VOCD discretization.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous-time periodic stabilization is approached indirectly through discretization plus sequential pole assignment.

status_evidence.title: Parametric Pole Assignment and Robust Pole Assignment for Discrete-Time Linear Periodic Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Complete parametric approach to pole assignment by periodic state feedback for discrete-time linear periodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Effective pole assignment algorithms exist for the discrete-time periodic case.

status_evidence.title: Robust and Minimum Norm Pole Assignment with Periodic State Feedback
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm computes periodic state feedback by minimization of condition numbers of closed-loop eigenvector matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Robust periodic-feedback pole assignment algorithms have been developed, mostly in discrete-time framework.
